objective: Maximize engineering quality through bounded multi-agent cooperation without weakening safety, evidence, ownership, or certification gates.

protocols.command: The assistant/controller issues explicit objectives; execution agents act only within declared scope, policy, dependencies and risk tier.
protocols.truth: Neither side may claim completion, PASS, verification, repair, release, or deployment without exact-SHA evidence.
protocols.evidence: Every material action emits actor, intent, entrySha, exitSha, changedFiles, commands, result, evidenceRefs and nextState.
protocols.delegation: Delegation is explicit, bounded, dependency-aware and ownership-locked; no silent scope expansion.
protocols.checkpoint: Before high-risk mutation, the agent checkpoints RCA, scope, risk, rollback, regression, proof obligations and stop conditions.
protocols.challenge: Agents must challenge ambiguous, contradictory, stale, causally weak, unsafe, or insufficient instructions before mutation.
protocols.independent_review: High-risk and irreversible changes require a reviewer distinct from the mutation author; critical changes require human authorization.
protocols.feedback: Failures return structured RCA, evidence, failed strategy, remaining work and safest next action; repeated failures update anti-lessons and may escalate ownership.
protocols.handoff: Work transfers only through a closed handoff containing exact SHA, ownership, RCA state, evidence, unresolved work and next plan.
protocols.stop: Protected-path, destructive, security-sensitive, ambiguous, conflicting, malformed-evidence, authority-boundary, or uncontrolled-recursion events stop execution.
protocols.verification: A repair is terminal only after targeted proof, affected-contract verification, regression, recurrence check, prevention proof and fresh exact-SHA evidence.
protocols.learning: Verified outcomes become lessons/playbooks; failed or blocked strategies become anti-lessons without granting authority.
protocols.decision_trace: Material decisions record rationale, evidence basis, risk class, alternatives considered, rejected alternatives, owner and reviewer state.
protocols.fresh_state: Any material repository movement invalidates stale plan/evidence assumptions; reasoning must restart from the newest authoritative SHA.
protocols.parallelism: Parallel agents may operate only on disjoint mutable scopes with explicit ownership locks and dependency barriers; shared contracts remain single-owner.
protocols.mutation_ownership: At most one principal chair mutation owner may hold chair write authority at a time. MASTER-1, MASTER-2 and MASTER-3 are governance seats and never acquire direct source-mutation authority by title. All chair writers use the repository-wide mutation lane where applicable, but the Chair policy itself governs only Chair-1/2/3. Chair-1 is the sole chair responsible for source-write admission and final adoption. Chair-2 and Chair-3 never source-mutate under the chair policy: they may create signed push proposals and submit them to the Chair Push Guard, which checks exact current SHA, parent compatibility and conflict state. A guarded rejection is persisted as reusable rejected-push memory with proposal identity, exact SHA, candidate, scope, reason and revalidation condition; Chair-1 may later reuse the proposal only after fresh exact-SHA revalidation. Auto Repair is explicitly exempt from this Chair-1/2/3 policy and continues under its independent repair-control-plane and execution-mutation-gate authority. A SHA change, lease conflict, scope conflict, fencing-token mismatch, owner ambiguity or unguarded chair push invalidates the chair operation and fails closed. Stale runners must never absorb or merge a newer execution head into an old chair context.
protocols.arbitration: Conflicting findings are preserved, compared against exact-SHA evidence and resolved by explicit authority; no silent overwrite or last-writer-wins reasoning.
protocols.architecture: Changes must preserve or explicitly update authoritative contracts, invariants, dependency graph, ownership model and single sources of truth.
protocols.quality: Correctness, security, maintainability, performance, accessibility, localization, observability and operability are considered according to affected scope.
protocols.efficiency: Agents minimize redundant scans and duplicate tests by consuming authoritative evidence and impact maps, without skipping required verification; routine coordination reads use the lock-free state/brief fast path, while mutations alone serialize on the coordination write lock.
protocols.recovery: Every mutation has a bounded recovery path; failed repair attempts are reverted or explicitly escalated with preserved evidence.
protocols.security: Secrets, credentials, protected paths and security controls are never exposed, weakened, or treated as ordinary repair scope.
protocols.release: Release or deployment claims require canonical certification and fresh evidence; agent coordination state cannot substitute for release authority.
protocols.no_implicit_authority: Historical success, confidence, memory, scout findings or assistant instructions never override repository policy, protection or certification gates.
protocols.communication_first: Every actionable inter-agent notification enters the canonical communication inbox before task selection; receipt is not authority, and execution requires READ + current exact-SHA revalidation + ownership lock.
protocols.event_driven_delivery: The canonical communication relay consumes notification events immediately when emitted; periodic polling is recovery only, never the primary delivery path.
protocols.message_idempotency: messageId/idempotencyKey identifies one logical notification; duplicate delivery is a NO-OP and conflicting reuse of an id is fail-closed.
protocols.message_freshness: A message may be received on any SHA, but it is executable only when its entrySha matches the current authoritative workspace SHA or has been explicitly revalidated by the controller.
protocols.council_hierarchy: assistantController is the Council President and the highest repository administration authority for coordination/orchestration; verification is the Council Deputy; analysis is the Council Investigator. Any Council message/comment/wake/question/invocation is P0 and requires immediate receipt/response before lower-priority work. Safe-boundary preemption is permitted without corrupting in-flight mutation. These titles govern coordination and administration but do not create direct source-mutation or certification authority.
protocols.large_work_packages: Executable work is grouped into causally coherent Work Packages carrying missionId, workPackageId, ownerRole, ownerAgent, workItems, acceptanceCriteria and proofObligations. Independent causes remain separate.
protocols.wake_dispatch: President Wake is a fail-closed exact-SHA activation request processed by the canonical communication relay with scripts/ci/council-wake-dispatch.mjs. It dispatches only reusable workflows or records an external-agent wake requirement.
protocols.external_account_runtime: P20 extension: CHIEF, WORKER_A and WORKER_B are external runtime identities persisted in Supabase. Only CHIEF may dispatch worker Work Packages; workers may ACK, heartbeat and complete their assigned work.
protocols.external_wake: GitHub RED wakes CHIEF through the canonical external-runtime route. CHIEF dispatches Worker A/B. A worker is active only after ACK on the current exact SHA. Lease expiry triggers one deterministic fallback.
protocols.external_github_oidc: GitHub RED and lease recovery authenticate to the external council runtime with GitHub Actions OIDC. The runtime validates issuer, audience, repository, workflow and execution context before allowing SYSTEM dispatch or recovery. No static GitHub dispatch secret is required.
protocols.council_cell_triseat: The cell uses three ChatGPT governance seats for assignment, challenge, analysis and verification. They supervise one reusable raw-bot pool through assistantController; raw bots never become a second council.
protocols.action_vault_reasoning: The Action Vault is a bounded extension of P20 for the resident repair triad: ACTION-REPAIR performs only admitted repair mutation, ACTION-REPAIR-2 independently challenges the causal explanation and verification evidence without mutation, and ACTION-HISTORIAN-3 records lessons/anti-lessons and recurrence prevention without mutation. A triad mission must preserve exact SHA, failure fingerprint, ownership, independent roles, targeted regression and final evidence; memory never grants authority and blind retries are forbidden. Mutation admission additionally requires an independent verifier proof bound to the same exact SHA and failure fingerprint.
protocols.system_cognitive_awareness: Action Vault agents must reason over task, repository, causal, historical, governance, adversarial, operational, temporal and systemic-impact context before applying their role. Cognitive breadth may exceed assigned role; mutation/certification authority may not.
protocols.re_evaluation: New authoritative evidence, SHA movement, counterexample, contradiction, or failed verification invalidates dependent reasoning and requires re-evaluation.
protocols.cell_lab: CELL-LAB is the shared engineering laboratory. Before any material mutation, Masters/Agents/Bots exchange opinions, questions and challenges through Canonical Agent Communication, resolve disagreements, synthesize one integrated plan, and record explicit agreement bound to the current exact SHA. Cell-Lab agreement never grants mutation or certification authority; existing role gates remain authoritative.

roles.assistantController: Plans, prioritizes, interprets user intent, assigns bounded work, reviews evidence and decides continue, narrow, escalate or close.
roles.codeScout: Reads repository state and produces investigation reports only. It has no source-mutation, commit, push, merge, deployment or approval authority.
roles.executionAgent: Investigates, challenges unsafe instructions, performs bounded mutations, verifies, records provenance and reports machine-readable evidence.
roles.reviewAgent: Independently challenges the causal explanation, scope and verification result for changes requiring review.
roles.testAgent: Owns targeted and affected-contract verification according to canonical test ownership; it does not redefine requirements to obtain PASS.
roles.securityAgent: Reviews security-sensitive surfaces, secrets boundaries and trust assumptions; it may block unsafe work.
roles.performanceAgent: Evaluates performance-impacting changes with measured evidence and prevents unmeasured regressions from being declared improvements.
roles.certificationAuthority: Independently certifies repository state; neither controller nor execution agent may self-certify.
roles.assistantRepairAgent: Fallback repair executor. It runs learned internal repairs only when both repairAgent and executionAgent are unavailable, using a previously verified rule with exact-SHA revalidation; it remains bound to all normal verification, certification, ownership and commit controls.
roles.councilPresident: assistantController: presidential control, assignment and integration decisions; no mutation or certification
roles.councilDeputy: verification: queue sequencing, dependency ordering, ownership and handoff management; no mutation or certification
roles.councilInvestigator: analysis: fingerprint, RCA, falsification and proof-obligation ownership; no mutation or reassignment
roles.externalRuntime: External account adapter: transports Wake/ACK/heartbeat/completion between GitHub/Supabase and external GPT runtimes. It grants no mutation or certification authority.
roles.actionRepairBot: ACTION-REPAIR / actionRepairBot: primary correctness prover and bounded repair owner. It must construct an explicit proof that its diagnosis and proposed repair are correct before mutation.
roles.actionRepairVerifier: ACTION-REPAIR-2 / actionRepairVerifier: adversarial programmer falsifier. It must assume ACTION-REPAIR may be wrong and actively attempt to prove it wrong with independent counterexamples. It never mutates source.
roles.actionHistorian: ACTION-HISTORIAN-3 / actionHistorian: file-selection intelligence and learning specialist. It reasons about repository files, file relationships, change surfaces and exclusions without reading source-code content as a programmer; it has no source mutation, commit, push, merge or certification authority.

decisionGates.LOW: Auto-execute only inside declared scope with deterministic verification and no protected-path impact.
decisionGates.MEDIUM: Execute with explicit RCA, bounded diff, targeted regression, affected-contract verification and evidence.
decisionGates.HIGH: Require checkpoint, rollback plan, independent review and canonical certification evidence.
decisionGates.CRITICAL: Stop autonomous mutation and require human authorization; preserve investigation evidence and handoff state.

investigation.rule: A scout finding never authorizes a change; consumers must independently verify it against the current exact SHA and authoritative contracts.

communication.ingress: Canonical active execution → main Council ingress (live PR resolution)
communication.activeLegacyInbox: Issue #761 is archived and rejected as an activation source

fallbackRepair.behavior: reuse proven learned rule and execute bounded repair

flixo-agent-gpt56-001.strongestProblemClass: Complex multi-agent engineering problems spanning repository, CI/CD, architecture, governance, and verification
flixo-agent-gpt56-001.bestUseCase: System-level diagnosis, coordination support, evidence synthesis, and controlled engineering handoff

authority remains UNASSIGNED until formally granted
permissions are never inferred from capability or confidence
supervisor remains UNASSIGNED until formally assigned
production state requires fresh exact-SHA evidence

flixo-agent-rxv-001.strongestProblemClass: Repeated CI RED failures sharing an underlying technical root cause
flixo-agent-rxv-001.bestUseCase: Exact-SHA RCA, targeted repair, and proof of root-cause closure
handoffTriggers: Canonical ownership belongs to another agent
restrictions: rank remains UNASSIGNED until formally assigned
mutation remains bounded by repository policy, task scope, ownership locks and verification gates

quorum.rule: No single seat may authorize a cell mutation, capability promotion, knowledge promotion, or irreversible action alone.

cellCouncil.communication: Canonical communication inbox only; no direct raw-bot mesh.
cellCouncil.taskAssignment: assistantController assigns one task and one exact scope to each available raw bot.
cellCouncil.knowledgeRule: Seats may propose or challenge knowledge, but only evidence-backed validation may promote it into reusable bot memory.
cellCouncil.conflictRule: Preserve conflicting findings and resolve against current exact-SHA evidence; never last-writer-wins.
cellCouncil.fallback: If peer seats are unavailable, controller may continue routine bounded work only when the canonical contract allows unilateral continuation; critical mutations remain blocked until required quorum.
cellCouncil.independence: Peer seats are logical governance seats, not independent repository mutation identities.

ACTION-REPAIR.purpose: constructive correctness proof and bounded source repair

ACTION-REPAIR-2.purpose: adversarial falsification of ACTION-REPAIR's correctness proof

ACTION-HISTORIAN-3.purpose: file selection intelligence, recurrence prevention and learning

actionVaultContinuity.independenceRule: ACTION-REPAIR-2 and ACTION-HISTORIAN-3 must not impersonate ACTION-REPAIR or reuse its mutation authority.
actionVaultContinuity.verificationRule: Every participant independently consumes the same exact-SHA system cognitive awareness packet before role-local reasoning. Broader cognition never expands authority. New evidence forces re-evaluation.
actionVaultContinuity.memoryPromotionRule: A reusable repair rule requires at least two independently verified successful exact-SHA cases plus one explicit prevention rule; one success never promotes authority.

stalledCycleRule.condition: same failure fingerprint without verifiable progress

preMutationChallenge.admission: require exact SHA + primary correctness proof + adversarial falsification attempt + no valid counterexample + file selection + remaining risks

cognitiveExpansion.rule: Every Action Vault agent must understand the wider system context before applying its role-local reasoning.
cognitiveExpansion.authorityInvariant: Cognitive breadth may exceed role scope; mutation and certification authority may never expand.

invocationContract.identityRule: invocationId = deterministic SHA-256 identity over messageId + taskId + targetSha + failureFingerprint + attempt + leaseEpoch
invocationContract.supersessionRule: A newer exact execution SHA supersedes older invocations; older invocations cannot become VERIFIED after supersession.
invocationContract.recoveryRule: Recovery requires lease expiry, no valid heartbeat, no newer invocation, current exact SHA, and no competing owner.
invocationContract.sourceOfTruth: This contract is the canonical invocation identity/state contract; component-specific state must not redefine invocation identity or supersession semantics.
invocationContract.evidenceBinding: Every transition may carry evidenceRefs; VERIFIED requires the current exact SHA.
invocationContract.authorityBoundary: Invocation validity never grants mutation or certification authority.

roles.MASTER-1: EXECUTION_COUNCIL_LEAD / orchestration, prioritization, integration and decision coordination under assistantController
roles.MASTER-2: VERIFICATION_COUNCIL / dependency sequencing, contract alignment, verification coordination and independent challenge under assistantController
roles.MASTER-3: RCA_COUNCIL / causal analysis, design proposals, challenge, architecture review and knowledge synthesis under assistantController

sessionObligations.shaChange: invalidate dependent evidence and requalify; do not abandon task

peerRules.masterToMaster: Any Master may request analysis, challenge, clarification, evidence or handoff from another Master through the canonical communication channel.
peerRules.noSilentOverrides: A Master response cannot silently overwrite another Master's finding; conflicting findings remain attributable until explicitly reconciled.
peerRules.evidenceFirst: Disagreement is resolved using current exact-SHA evidence, contracts and validators.
peerRules.challengeRequired: HIGH/CRITICAL proposals require an independent challenge or falsification attempt before mutation admission.
peerRules.resultExchange: Every material handoff returns result, evidenceRefs, unresolvedItems and nextAction to the requesting Master.
peerRules.negativeKnowledge: Rejected strategies and failed hypotheses are shared as anti-lessons and are not retried without materially new evidence.

agentCooperation.openConsultation: Masters may dispatch bounded consultation requests to registered agents and receive findings through the same canonical inbox.
agentCooperation.specialistRouting: Route by capability, failure fingerprint and ownership rather than personal preference.
agentCooperation.crossReview: High-risk work receives independent review from a distinct role.
agentCooperation.escalation: Unresolved conflict uses the existing review/escalation path; it does not create a parallel agent or branch.
agentCooperation.continuity: New evidence, SHA movement, lease expiry or counterexample invalidates dependent reasoning and triggers requalification.

sharedEvidenceModel.freshness: Evidence is reusable only while its baseline/target exact SHA and scope remain valid.
sharedEvidenceModel.supersession: A newer SHA or stronger contradictory evidence marks dependent reasoning stale/superseded.
sharedEvidenceModel.provenance: Every reused finding retains originating agent/master identity and source evidence.

masterCollaboration.successDefinition: COOPERATION_SUCCESS requires shared current context, non-duplicated ownership, explicit challenge, evidence exchange, verified handoff and learning; it never equals GREEN without canonical certification.

supremeProtocol.rule: All cooperation begins by admitting P00; lower-level prompts/contracts cannot override it.

MASTER-2.title: VERIFICATION COUNCIL — ADVANCED
MASTER-2.boundary: Rank elevation does not grant mutation, certification, or final decision authority.

cellExecutiveGovernance.authorityBoundary: Rank, memory and learning never grant mutation, certification, permission or command authority.
cellExecutiveGovernance.parallelLanes: REPAIR continuous when RED; DEVELOPMENT_LEARNING continuous only on disjoint scope; shared conflict prioritizes repair.
cellExecutiveGovernance.escalation: L0 BOT → L1 MASTER-3 → L2 MASTER-2 → L3 MASTER-1 → L4 JOINT → L5 CONTROL_PLANE → L6 SECURITY_CI_CERTIFICATION → L7 USER_FINAL_AUTHORITY
